m: śuṣka mf(ā)n. dried, dried up, dry, arid, parched, shrivelled, emaciated, shrunk, withered, sere, RV. &c. &c.
useless, fruitless, groundless, vain, unprofitable, empty, Mn.; MBh. &c.
śuṣka m. N. of a man (a relative of Sukha-varman; cf. śuṣkaṭa-varman), Rājat.
śuṣka n. (and m. g. ardharcādi) anything dry (e.g. dry wood, dry cow-dung &c.), RV.; Viṣṇ.
śuṣka Nom. (only inf. śuṣkitum) to become dry, Divyāv.
a: śuṣka p. p. [śuṣ-kta] 1 Dry, dried up; śākhāyāṃ śuṣkaṃ kariṣyāmi Mk. 8. 2 Parched up, sear. 3 Shrivelled, shrunk up, emaciated. 4 Feigned, pretended, mock; kāminaḥ sma kurute karabhorūrhāri śuṣkaruditaṃ ca sukhe'pi Śi. 10. 69. 5 Empty, vain, useless, unproductive; M. 2. 6 Groundless, causeless. 7 Offensive, harsh; tasmai nākuśalaṃ brūyānna śuṣkāṃ giramīrayet Ms. 11. 35. Comp. — aṃga a. emaciated. — (gī) a lizard. — annaṃ rice in the husk. — ārdraṃ dry ginger. — kalahaḥ 1 a vain or groundless quarrel. 2 a mock quarrel; Mu. 3. — vairaṃ groundless enmity. — vraṇaṃ a healed wound, scar.
